key_insight: A 3D thermomechanical model of AA2024 aluminum–Cu-DHP copper radial friction welding predicts asymmetric heating and localized deformation near the interface.
engineering_relevance: The model helps interpret thermal and deformation responses in dissimilar aluminum–copper welds under the studied processing conditions.
method: Coupled 3D finite element modelling in ANSYS Workbench 2023 R1 at 1,400 rpm and 30 MPa.
Optical metallography and Vickers microhardness characterization.
Comparison with thermocouple measurements and aluminum-side TMAZ width.
evidence_signal: Predictions included a 750 °C interface peak, 0.0177 equivalent plastic strain, and 0.130 mm maximum displacement; temperature and TMAZ-width comparisons supported the model, while measured TMAZ hardness reached approximately 157 HV.
watch_item: Friction and radiation assumptions, omitted latent heat, and absent microstructural kinetics limit interpretation; hardness does not directly validate strain or identify phases.
paper_title: Three-Dimensional Thermomechanical Analysis of Radial Friction Welding of Dissimilar Copper-Aluminum Alloys: Finite Element Modelling and Experimental Validation
